The existence of the art of transforming **imperfect metals** <note>In alchemical theory, "imperfect" or "base" metals like lead, tin, or copper were thought to be "sick" versions of "perfect" metals.</note> into **perfect ones** <note>Referring to gold and silver, which were considered chemically stable and "mature."</note> has always been the <note>original: "Zankapfel," an idiom meaning "apple of discord" or a bone of contention.</note> bone of contention among scholars; and not infrequently, it had to endure being judged by people who did not even have enough healthy brain in their heads to associate a correct concept with the word: **Alchemy**. ...but not its reality. They put forward the following opinion, which, however, experience and reason already refute: because Nature has drawn a veil over that most refined **alkaline earth** <note>In alchemical theory, this refers to a specific, purified mineral "salt" or "body" thought to be essential for the growth of metals.</note> which she requires, in addition to the **formative water** <term>original: "Webungswasser" - literally "weaving water," a term for the liquid medium or mercurial substance in which metals are "woven" or generated in the earth.</term> of metals, for their creation; and because man knows neither its true nature nor the weight with which it must be combined with that water; thus the reality of the **art of making gold and silver** <note>The alchemical practices of chrysopeia (gold-making) and argyropeia (silver-making).</note> will remain impossible as long as the secret earth required for it remains a mystery to mankind. 

Following this pattern, one still finds many doubters, who differ from one another only according to the concepts they have formed regarding the natural birth and **ennobling of metals** <note>The process by which "base" metals like lead were believed to naturally mature into "noble" metals like gold over vast periods of time.</note>. This was its ancient fate, and its current one is not a hair better. Scholars of all ranks, professional **analytical chemists** <term>original: "Scheidekünstler," literally "artists of separation," an early term for chemists or assayers who specialized in breaking substances down into their components.</term>, and even those wretched creatures, the writers of novels and comedies, have the audacity to mistreat this great art, to make it look ridiculous, and thereby still the rumblings of their own shriveled stomachs <note>A biting metaphorical suggestion that these writers only mock alchemy to produce popular, profitable works to pay for their meals.</note>. 

In general, it belongs nowadays to those things which one must flatly deny, if one

...whenever one wants to earn the reputation of a bright mind. For what a miserable figure a **fashionable scholar** <note>The author uses "Modegelehrter" to mock the trend-following academics of the Enlightenment who dismissed traditional or esoteric knowledge.</note> of our time would make, if he only let it be known that he believes the Bible to be God’s Word; that he believes no upright man can be imagined without **religion**; that he believes **Moses** was no imposter and **Christ** was more than just a good, wise, charitable, and philanthropic man! And how terribly the dictatorial scholars would first lash him with special rods if he were to say out loud: "I am convinced of the existence of **Higher Chemistry** <note>Refers to Alchymia, or spiritual alchemy, as opposed to "lower" common chemistry.</note> and **Magic**; I am convinced that both sciences are sisters of revealed and natural religion, and that the foundation of all **philosophy** lies in these sciences."

Suppose a father promises his son that he will buy him the desired beautiful musical instrument as soon as he can play it. Is the son then not bound to fulfill this **condition** first, before his wish is to be granted? ### 23.

Now it is certain once and for all that the **true philosophical matter** <note>original Latin: "vera materia sophica." In alchemy, "philosophical" matter refers to the refined, spiritualized substance rather than common raw materials.</note>, the **proper subject of our art** <note>original Latin: "debitum subjectum artis nostrae." The "subject" is the starting material for the alchemical process.</note>, is a mineral; however, because there are so very many minerals, this specific one is very difficult to recognize. For as can be seen from the writings of the Sages, they speak of all metals and minerals at once, as if they were a single metal and mineral. It is remarkable that they always categorize them together as many different kinds, yet they understand them as only a single thing, because everything is hidden in one, and one is hidden in all. From this, it can be concluded that it must be a mineral in which all the others lie buried in their essence, but especially where gold and silver lie buried according to their potential.

**Answer.** The tincture with which Nature tinges gold is, beyond all doubt, an exceedingly pure, subtle, spiritual, fixed, and incombustible sulfur, through whose power gold was born in the womb of the earth. # Appendix
## of several axioms for the students of wisdom.

Nature is a spirit of light, which was substantially created by God and received a body, which is nevertheless invisible and intangible, and lies hidden in all created things. <note>In this context, "Nature" is not just the outdoors, but a divine, living force that permeates all matter.</note>

->2.<-

The body of nature, however, is nothing other than the <term>central salt</term> <note>original: "centralische Salz." In alchemy, "Salt" represents the principle of fixity and the physical body.</note> hidden in every thing, in which <term>at the root</term> <note>original Latin: "radicaliter"</note> rest the <term>sulfur</term> <note>original: "Schwefel"</note> and <term>mercury</term> <note>original: "Mercurius"</note> as brothers of the salt: and yet it is no <term>composite</term> <note>original: "Kompositum"; a mixture of different things.</note>, but all three together are an entirely simple, uniform essence, even though it consists of three. <note>This refers to the "Tria Prima" or Three Primes. Alchemists believed all matter was composed of Salt (body), Sulfur (soul), and Mercury (spirit).</note>

->3.<-

This <term>central salt</term> is the body of nature, in which the properties of all things lie hidden, and it is <term>incorruptible</term> <note>original: "incorruptibel"; eternal and unable to decay.</note> even though the bodies brought forth through the <term>central salt</term> are <term>corruptible</term> <note>original: "corruptibel"; subject to decay, change, and death.</note>.

### 34.

# Account
## of the Life of Theophrastus Paracelsus.

Theophrastus Paracelsus Bombast von Hohenheim, Doctor of Philosophy and Medicine at the University of Basel, came from a noble family and was born in 1464 <note>Historical records typically place Paracelsus's birth around 1493; the date 1464 provided here may be a transcription error or a variation in earlier biographical traditions.</note> in Einsiedeln, a village not far from Zurich. His father introduced him to the sciences from his youth and, as he grew older, sent him to the University of Salamanca in Spain, where he remained for a considerable time. He is said to have been a student of the old master of the arts <term>Kunstbesizer: a term often used to describe those who possessed the "Great Art" of alchemy</term> Salomon Trismosin, which is evident from his preface to this *Wishing Hat* <note>original: "Wünschhütlein"; likely a reference to a specific alchemical work or a metaphorical title for a collection of transformative knowledge</note>, wherein he says that he read with profit the writings of a Thuringian monk (presumably Basilius Valentinus). After completing his studies, he undertook extensive travels through Asia, Africa, and Europe.

<summary>This page introduces the life of the famous physician and alchemist Paracelsus, detailing his birth in Switzerland, his education in Spain, and his early influences, including the legendary alchemists Salomon Trismosin and Basilius Valentinus.</summary>
<keywords>Theophrastus Paracelsus, biography, Einsiedeln, University of Salamanca, Salomon Trismosin, alchemy, Basilius Valentinus, history of medicine</keywords>

# Preface

## By Philippus Theophrastus Paracelsus of

### Hohenheim.

Although I have indeed described and noted various things in our *Archidoxis* <note>The *Archidoxis* (The Greater Doctrines) is one of Paracelsus's most influential works, focusing on the chemical extraction of medicinal virtues</note> and other writings that deal with chemistry and medicine, I did so in such a way that the pearl might not be cast before swine <note>A biblical reference (Matthew 7:6) indicating that sacred or secret knowledge should be protected from the unworthy</note>. However, I have recorded the present information for my own reference, so that the knowledge of such high secrets may not fall into oblivion for me, since the true <term>universals</term> <note>Broadly acting sovereign remedies</note> and <term>arcana</term> <note>Secret, powerful healing essences</note>—both in chemistry and in medicine—cannot be prepared without the correct manual procedures <note>original: "Handgriffe" — the specific physical techniques and manipulations required in a laboratory</note>. Therefore, I have found it necessary to write this down correctly, especially how the true <term>quintessence</term> <note>The "fifth essence" or the purest, most concentrated medicinal force within a substance</note> can be enhanced step by step. This is not described according to our old custom, as used in our previous books which we published in a philosophical and <term>kabbalistic</term> <note>Here referring to a coded, mystical style of writing intended to be understood only by the spiritually enlightened or "pious"</note> manner, so that only the pious

<summary>In this preface, Paracelsus explains that he is writing down his practical chemical secrets for his own records to prevent them from being forgotten, moving away from his usual cryptic and mystical style of writing.</summary>

might find it; I have hidden such things from the scornful, the foolish, and the godless, so that those greedy for gold <note>original: "Goldſüchtigen"</note> might also beat their brains against it. However, we have written down this present work as a record for ourselves, so that it may be passed down to our children after us, enabling them to come to the aid of the sick and infirm in their times of need. 

The reason I wrote nothing clearly for the Galenic doctors <note>original: "Doctoribus Galenicis" — physicians who followed the ancient Greek theories of Galen, whose reliance on "humors" Paracelsus vehemently rejected</note> in my previous writings is this: so that their ignorance <note>original: "Ignoranz"</note> might not be reinforced, but rather that they must wander far and wide within their own minds searching for the truth. They would dearly love to possess this secret, yet they wish to keep their hands delicate and soft, refusing to dirty them with coal <note>A reference to the physical, "dirty" work of the alchemical furnace</note>; instead, they prefer to sit in soft chairs, eat and drink well, and rest in soft beds.

# Chapter I.

## Regarding the **Separation of the Elements** <term>Separation of the Elements: The alchemical process of isolating the four basic building blocks of matter—Earth, Air, Fire, and Water—to reveal the pure substance hidden within.</term>, how and from what the true **Quintessence** <term>Quintessence: The 'fifth essence' or the purest, most powerful medicinal core of a substance, believed to be free of the impurities of the physical elements.</term> is to be separated, and by what means?

---

I have said in my little book of the **Archidoxes** <note>original: *Archidoxorum*; This refers to one of Paracelsus's most famous works, which details the extraction of "mysteries" and medicines from natural substances.</note> regarding the **Separation of the Elements**, that in all things four are mixed together among one another, and that among these four, only one is fixed and perfect; and that this one is the **predestined element** <note>original: *elementum praedestinatum*; the specific part of a substance that contains its unique, divinely appointed purpose or healing power.</note>, within which the true Quintessence dwells and exists. The other elements are imperfect: yet that one element is strong enough to **tincture** <term>Tincture: In this sense, to 'tinge' or imbue a substance with a specific quality or medicinal virtue, effectively transforming its nature.</term> and **qualify** <note>original: *qualificiren*; to determine or alter the specific properties and temperament of a substance.</note> these imperfect ones, each according to its own kind. For example, in some substances the element of **water** predominates <note>original: *prädominiret*; meaning the element of water has the strongest influence over the object's characteristics.</note>...

# Chapter VII.
## How to prepare a true *Universal Medicine*,
## with which one can work wonders
## in all diseases.

To prepare a true *Universal Medicine* <note>original: "Universalmedicin"; a legendary "cure-all" or panacea sought by alchemists to heal any physical or spiritual ailment.</note>, with which one can work wonders in all diseases, the great Creator created the grapevine and our daily bread for this purpose, with which all people are refreshed. # Chapter One.

-> In what does the life and multiplication <-
-> of creatures consist? <-

In the three <term>kingdoms of nature</term> <note>The three kingdoms are the animal, vegetable, and mineral realms.</note> there is a single spiritual essence, which animates their bodies and from which they receive their nourishment. This single spiritual essence originates from the <term>sidereal region</term> <note>The starry or celestial realm; in early modern science, it was believed that the stars influenced the growth and life of things on Earth.</note> and is incessantly communicated to the air, which then, acting as a <term>vehicle</term> <note>A medium or carrier.</note>, delivers it to those three kingdoms of nature. At the same time, however, there lies within creation and in all creatures a certain hidden attractive power, by which they are able most eagerly to take those heavenly outpourings into themselves.

Kingdoms of nature, spiritual essence, sidereal region, vehicle, creation, attractive power

<summary>This page introduces the foundational concept of a universal spiritual essence that originates in the stars and sustains all life on Earth through the air. It explains that all creatures possess a magnetic-like ability to draw this heavenly influence into themselves to live and grow.</summary>

<keywords>kingdoms of nature, spiritual essence, sidereal region, vital force, creation, attractive power, cosmology</keywords>

After these presupposed principles of the **generation** <note>original: *Generation*. The process of purifying and refining a substance after it has been broken down.</note> of bodies, as the two natural means. The first of these returns the body to its **universality** <note>original: *Universalität*. The internal essence or "blueprint" that makes a thing what it is (e.g., the "form" of lead vs. the "form" of gold).</note> from itself and determining it into another form according to one's will. Once this form is separated from it, it is then also easy to divide the **constitutive principles** <note>original: *konstitutiven Principien*. After its purification and **calcination** <term>Calcination</term> <note>The process of heating a substance to high temperatures in the presence of air to reduce it to a brittle powder or ash.</note>, separate it into the **volatile** and **fixed** parts; take the **spirit** from the **earth** and cleanse it of all watery and earthy parts; prepare it for the **philosophical solution** <note>The process of dissolving the solid "body" into a liquid "spirit" using a specialized alchemical solvent.</note>; furthermore, through the proper manipulations, take the waters from the earth—that is: separate our pure **solar earth** <note>The refined, essential substance of the matter, often associated with the "sulfur" or the "sun" within the mineral.</note> and remove the metallic form entirely from it; for this would ruin everything if you neglected to do so. If this is properly...

...performed; thus bring the spirit gradually back to its earth, which will most greedily draw the spirit to itself. After the completed **imbibitions** <term>imbibitions</term> <note>The process of "feeding" or soaking a solid substance with a liquid (spirit) until it is saturated and the two are unified.</note>, the spirit will become a body, and the body a spirit, and both will become one. Follow Nature; for when the **saturation** <term>saturation</term> has occurred and our **double eagle** <note>An alchemical symbol for the union of the volatile (spirit) and the fixed (earth), or the process of distillation and sublimation.</note> wants to lift its wings, then catch it and preserve it with caution, because you have now obtained the **dry water of the Sages** <note>original: "d. W." (der Weisen); "dry water" refers to the philosophical mercury, a substance that acts like a liquid but does not wet the hands.</note>, which does not wet the hands and possesses the power to regenerate all metallic bodies. Give it its proper **ferment** <term>ferment</term> <note>A substance (often gold or silver) added to the finished "Stone" to determine its final direction and stabilize its power.</note> and follow the signposts of Nature.

And since I have often had to express myself very briefly in this book, the writings of **Flamel**, **Hermes**, **Hortulanus**, **Kelley**, and **Hollandus** <note>A list of foundational alchemical authors: Nicolas Flamel, Hermes Trismegistus, Hortulanus (author of a famous commentary on the Emerald Tablet), Edward Kelley (associate of John Dee), and the Hollandus brothers.</note> can provide you with additional instruction; but I especially recommend to you the **Table of the immortal Hermes** <note>Refers to the *Tabula Smaragdina* or Emerald Tablet, the brief, cryptic text said to contain the secret of the "one thing" that creates the universe.</note>, which contains the true foundation of the entire **Hermetic art** <term>Hermetics</term>. Learn above all things to understand precisely the natural mixture of bodies; investigate how and through what means and manipulations one part of a body can be released from the other; then the practical execution of these instructions will be very easy for you, and you can be assured of a good outcome for your undertaking.

<meta>This page concludes the author's preface or introductory remarks, transitioning from the list of alchemical authorities (Flamel, Hermes, etc.) mentioned on the previous page to a final moral and practical warning for the aspiring alchemist.</meta>

-><image-desc>A small decorative woodcut (fleuron) with floral and scrollwork designs is centered between the page number and the start of the text.</image-desc><-

...found people over time to be quite different than how I judged them then. For the God-fearing and industrious <term>naturalist</term> <note>original: "Naturforscher"; in the 18th century, this term referred to a student of the natural sciences, often including alchemy and hermetic philosophy.</note>, the few dark spots of my principles will very soon unfold, especially since I have presented the essential parts of the whole Art without any reservation. Let him only follow Nature as faithfully as she does in the bringing forth of her creations, and always work with a pure heart and washed hands, in order to separate the impure from the pure and to bring the latter to the highest perfection. 

But woe to the man who sets his hand to the work and yet is in no way called to it; who lacks the fear of God and the fundamental knowledge of nature and <term>chemical manipulations</term> <note>original: "chimische Manipulationen"; the practical laboratory operations such as distillation, sublimation, and calcination.</note> required beforehand, and who only wishes to possess such an inestimable <term>treasure</term> <note>original: "Kleinod"; literally a jewel or gem, often used to describe the Philosopher's Stone.</note> like a child reaching into a lucky dip <note>original: "Glückshafen"; a historical term for a raffle or lottery jar found at public fairs.</note> for a piece of money! He is a fool! Nor should he venture upon the sea to fetch the Golden Fleece of Colchis <note>In Greek mythology, the Golden Fleece was the prize sought by Jason and the Argonauts; in alchemy, it is a common metaphor for the ultimate secret of the Great Work.</note> who lacks a speculative genius and the very specific temperament required for this undertaking. His good intentions, which bid him hoist the sails, will put his ship in danger and finally dash it against the cliffs of poverty. 

But whoever is so fortunate as to find the Stone, visible to only a few, for which the signpost has here been set up, let him worship his good Creator with double thanks. Let him glorify His great name and not forget the needy who sigh alongside and around him.

<summary>The author warns that alchemy requires both spiritual purity and practical expertise, cautioning that those seeking only wealth without the proper "naturel" will face ruin. It concludes with an exhortation to use the successful discovery of the Stone for charitable ends.</summary>

<keywords>naturalist, nature, chemical manipulations, Golden Fleece, poverty, Philosopher's Stone, charity, God-fearing</keywords>
